title: AgentDesktop Runtime API agentdesktop.runtime/1 (draft, PR1 read-only surface)

notSent.description: not_performed: true only when the Runtime (or the client, before sending) can prove this request sent no input and made no write with an outside effect, whether or not it reached the Runtime. Never true for a partial send, a timeout, a lost connection, a missing receipt or an unknown outcome. Not a licence to retry: a retry is judged again by authorization, Run state, stops, policy and the request ledger.

includeOffscreen.description: also minimized, hidden and other-Space windows; default on-screen only

source.description: commit the product was built from, or "unknown" outside a bundled build

gui.description: what the GUI execution backend supports, as the AI service reports it (ai-gui/v1 runtime_capabilities_result); absent while that service is not running

kind.description: virtual: a display the Runtime created and destroys; physical: one of the user's displays, attached; absent means virtual

startedAt.description: process start time; pid plus start time names one launch

title.description: null when the OS withholds titles (no Screen Recording grant)

physical.description: attach one of the user's own displays instead of creating a virtual one: nothing is created, window.bind needs windowId and never moves the window, app.launch is refused, desktop.destroy only drops the record; mutually exclusive with width/height

displayId.description: a physical display's ID; default the main display

elements.description: default true; needs a bound window

quitApps.description: apps launched onto the Desktop that were asked to quit

coverage.description: what this observation could see: the element read may be partial (truncated walk) or unavailable (deadline passed, a read of the Desktop still running) while the screenshot is complete

businessResult.description: delivery is not effect; a later observation or the caller establishes the effect

reason.description: why the action was not delivered, failed or has an unknown outcome; absent when delivered

lifetime.description: accepted only to refuse escalation explicitly

Principal.description: who the Runtime holds this connection to be (A4): from the credential shown in runtime.handshake, never from params

codeIdentityLevel.description: how far the Runtime can tell this connection's program from other processes of the user (A4 S2)

lifetime.description: accepted only to refuse escalation explicitly

cursor.description: resume with events.subscribe after=cursor: the sequence for a Run stream, the global cursor otherwise

PlatformRunEvent.description: the events the Runtime writes on every Run; RunEvent types with the prefix run., action. or stop. are these. The prefix unit. is the GUI unit's own (documented with the Explorer), other prefixes are reserved.

RunUnit.description: present only on kind unit: the GUI unit's own facts, beside the Run's phase/outcome/quiescence

UnitVerification.description: every predicate must hold on a fresh observation; each is a service.schema.json GuiVerification

agentName.description: one line of printable text, shown to the user as self-reported (no control, line-separator or bidi characters)

publisher.description: one line of printable text, shown to the user as self-reported (no control, line-separator or bidi characters)

CodeIdentity.description: what the Runtime read from the socket peer's kernel audit token (A4 S2), never from anything the client sends. verified: team-signed, hardened runtime, bound by its designated requirement; shared_interpreter: as verified but an interpreter whose every script shares it; same_user: nothing verifiable, only a process of this user; in_process: the host itself

requirement.description: the designated requirement every later connection of this client must satisfy
